items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I played with him with Maynard.

ctx.x: How did that situation develop? Who approached you? How did that come about?
The guy that played first trombone with Stan Kenton was playing in the band, Bobby Burgess. He had played with Stan Kenton. Then he played with Louis Jordan’s big band. Did you ever hear that band?
I can’t say that I have, no.

items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: when we did the trombone thing recently at the Blue Note with Bobby Burgess and Bill Watrous... they love to work together

ctx.x: To get a rehearsal in and scheduling.

It’s a job. When we did the trombone album, the trombone CD, we did that one thing, but we could never have that same group again. But we had good guys after that too, guys that weren’t on the CD. And when we did the trombone thing recently at the Blue Note with Bobby Burgess and Bill Watrous you know, those guys and Benny Powell, they love to work together so they’ll just about do anything they can to get to work in that group © Fillius Jazz Archive -24-
because they loved being there so much. But in general when you’ve got a group like that it’s hard to get that group together more than once. There always will be some change in there.
